answer:
Loom has no auto-scaling GPU cluster mode. I searched the docs and the feature list and found no such setting, so I won't invent a flag for it. Loom doesn't manage hardware. Each agent names a model with `model:`, and Loom calls that provider. Your three agents (Researcher, Writer, Editor) use `gemini-2.5-flash`, which is hosted, so scaling is the provider's job.

The nearest thing Loom does is a `routing` policy. It has `strategy: fallback` or `cost_aware`, so a call can fall back to another model or go to a cheaper one. It controls which model answers, not how much hardware runs it.

If you need to run your own GPUs, you would host the model yourself and point an agent at it. I'd have to check the docs before saying exactly how.

What are you after: lower cost, higher throughput, or keeping the data on your own machines? That decides what I'd suggest.
